inlineContent.text: Nothing in the engine imports anything but Foundation,
(three files) and
(one). Five files reach for platform C, and all five do it behind
: the terminal handler, the
check in
, the MCP play-test server, its stdio transport, and a thread-priority hint in
. Nothing in the parser, the turn pipeline, the rule table or the world state touches any of it.
The library therefore compiles for iOS unchanged, and the manifest declares
, so that is a configuration this package supports and builds rather
than a line you add yourself. The floor is
, the same
thing that sets the macOS 15 floor, and CI builds every product for
on each pull request. The terminal handler compiles there
and is useless there; a front end that never constructs one never pays for it.
That is all an iOS app does differently: it supplies its own handler, because
’s
check would hand it a console nobody reads.
